author: pallas, 1811
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록
habitat: 습지, 농경지, 해안 근처, 축축한 풀밭

months.note: 봄과 가을에 지나가며, 번식지에서는 6~7월에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 봄과 가을에 우리나라를 드물지 않게 지나가는 나그네새이다. 주로 곤충을 먹지만 겨울에는 풀씨를 먹으며, 여름에는 암수가 함께 지내다가 겨울에는 무리를 짓는다. 스칸디나비아반도와 동아시아의 툰드라에서 번식하는데, 습지·농경지·해안 근처나 축축한 풀밭의 살짝 팬 곳에 둥지를 틀고 알을 5~6개 낳는다. 겨울은 동남아시아에서 난다.

art.subject: Red-throated Pipit (Anthus cervinus), adult in spring (April–May): face, supercilium, throat and upper breast brick-pink to rusty-orange (strongest in males, paler in some females); crown, nape and back buff-brown boldly streaked black; rump also streaked; wings dark with pale-edged coverts forming two thin wing-bars; lower breast and belly pale yellowish-white; flanks with long black streaks; tail dark with whitish outer feathers; bill dark with a yellowish base; dark eye; pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: walking on damp ground, picking insects
art.scene: Korean spring migration: wet grassland and farmland near the coast; no people, buildings or text
views: adult in spring, side view walking on wet grass: brick-pink face, supercilium and throat, buff-brown back streaked black, pale yellowish-white belly, long black streaks on the flanks, pinkish legs
first-winter in autumn, side view on the ground: no pink, buff-brown upperparts heavily streaked black, whitish underparts with bold black streaks on breast and flanks, dark malar stripe
adult, seen from above on the ground: buff-brown crown, mantle and rump all streaked black, two thin pale wing-bars
art.build: Small, slim pipit, 15cm — about sparrow length but slimmer, with a horizontal walking posture. Bill slender and pointed, shorter than the head. Legs pinkish-brown, with a long hind claw. At rest the long tertials cover the primary tips almost completely. Tail medium-length and notched, with whitish outer feathers. Walks on wet grass and fields, often in small flocks.
avoid: Do not omit the brick-pink face and throat on spring adults; it is the species' namesake.
Do not paint a plain, unstreaked rump or back (Olive-backed or Buff-bellied Pipit); the rump is streaked.
Do not spread the pink onto the belly.
